title: One-Step Self-Assembling Lipopolymer Coatings Enable Direct Longitudinal Biosensing in Native Biological Matrices
summary: Sample-driven cross-reactivity remains a fundamental bottleneck for sensitive and selective biosensing in complex biological environments, particularly in microfluidic systems where high surface-to-volumes ratios amplify non-specific interactions. Here, we address this challenge with a one-step, biomimetic surface functionalization strategy based on engineered lipid-based nanocarriers that self-assemble within minutes into immunoassay-ready, antifouling interfaces that couple pegylated-lipid passivation with biorthogonal, site-specific probe conjugation. This approach enables rapid, tuneable, and reproducible surface functionalization, which suppresses sample-specific cross-reactivity even in undiluted serum, and supports direct, label-free digital biosensing assays directly in native biological environments. When integrated into an optofluidic platform combining digital in-line holography and microfluidics, this approach allows time-resolved quantification of tetraspanin-positive extracellular vesicle secretion dynamics from two-dimensional and three-dimensional lung cancer cell models using 50 μL of sample within 10 min, without isolation or purification. Because the presented surface functionalization proceeds via self-assembly rather than covalent surface modification, this one-step modular-approach is intrinsically decoupled from device fabrication and applies to both glass and PDMS, coating the entire microfluidic channel, thereby establishing a general route for integrating biomimetic nanostructures into robust, high-performance immunoassays, advancing biosensing beyond end-point measurements, and towards rapid and continuous real-time monitoring.

title: Critical slowing down in hive temperature does not provide actionable early warnings of honey bee colony collapse
summary: Early warning signals (EWS) based on critical slowing down (CSD) have been proposed as model-independent indicators of approaching ecological regime shifts and may help anticipate honeybee colony collapse. However, whether theoretically expected signals can be reliably observed and provide useful prediction in real-world systems remains uncertain. Here, we combine structural analysis, mechanistic modeling and longitudinal observations to assess the dynamical plausibility, detectability and predictive accuracy of CSD-based EWS for honeybee colony collapse. Our results show that the presence of EWS is not equivalent to successful prediction of the transition. The analyzed models exhibit regime shifts accompanied by CSD, but detecting these signals in finite and noisy observations requires longer and more densely sampled time series than typically available for practical monitoring. Moreover, in empirical temperature records, CSD-like trends were detectable but provided limited discrimination between colonies that subsequently collapsed and those that survived. Declining mean temperature provided slightly greater discrimination than conventional CSD indicators, although its predictive value remained modest. Non-Gaussian correlated noise and the imperfect correspondence between hive temperature and colony strength further constrained EWS performance. These findings show that EWS can exist at the dynamical level without becoming useful predictors at the observational level, at least for our case study, thus cautioning against treating CSD-based indicators as generic predictors of ecological collapse.

title: Integrated Stress Responses and ABCB11 Repression in Drug-Exposed Human Hepatocytes
summary: Drug-safety information systems must distinguish direct bile salt export pump (BSEP) inhibition from transcriptional changes in hepatic transport programs. We investigated whether repression of ABCB11, which encodes BSEP, tracks an integrated stress response (ISR) after accounting for dose and liver-identity proxies. We analyzed 197 human hepatocyte RNA-seq dose conditions for 50 compounds using compound-centered models and 2,000 compound-bootstrap resamples. The association remained negative after dose and 436-gene identity adjustment ($β=-0.288$; 95\% interval, $-0.416$ to $-0.127$), and after jointly adding global-expression, oxidative-stress and apoptosis scores ($β=-0.198$; $-0.342$ to $-0.039$). The adjusted partial correlation ($r=-0.422$) exceeded in absolute magnitude those obtained for all but 1 of 5,000 expression-matched and 16 of 5,000 expression- and variance-matched random six-gene sets. Several comparator transporters also declined, indicating that the association was not restricted to ABCB11. Adding an interpolated source-screen viability proxy to all controls retained a negative estimate but an interval including zero ($β=-0.190$; $-0.335$ to $0.009$; 152 conditions, 39 compounds). Exposure-restricted uncertainty likewise depended on identity adjustment. Published modules from 240 external microarray conditions for 80 perturbagens showed consistent stress--metabolic covariation, without gene-level replication. A separate assay/FDA audit exposed sparse joint coverage and source-dependent associations. Together, these analyses link hepatocyte stress to ABCB11 repression and provide a biologically grounded approach to integrating biochemical, transcriptional and regulatory evidence for drug-safety assessment.

title: Infection Spreading and Stochastic Extinction in Finite Spatially Inhomogeneous Susceptible-Infected-Susceptible and Susceptible-Infected-Recovered Systems
summary: Demographic fluctuations can drive finite epidemic populations into an absorbing disease-free state even when the corresponding infinite system supports sustained activity. By means of Monte Carlo simulations, we investigate how spatial coupling of two distinct subsystems modifies stochastic extinction and epidemic spreading in susceptible-infectious-susceptible (SIS) and susceptible-infectious-recovered (SIR) models on inhomogeneous two-dimensional square lattices. For isolated SIS systems, extinction times exhibit approximate power-law scaling near the epidemic threshold even for small systems. Traversal times characterize the distinct propagation dynamics of SIS and SIR infection clusters. We consider diffusively coupled regions with different transmission characteristics in coupled SIS-SIS, SIR-SIS, and SIR-SIR configurations. Invading fronts can reactivate a vulnerable SIS region after its initial infection has disappeared and establish a long-lived active epidemic state. This stabilization can be induced by either a sustained SIS source or a single transient SIR epidemic wave. Spatial correlation measurements support a mechanism in which the invading activity generates an extended correlated infectious population, effectively providing favorable initial conditions for renewed epidemic spreading. Correlations develop particularly strongly parallel to the subsystem interfaces. Decoupling the regions after some elapsed period demonstrates that autonomous persistence requires sufficient coupling time beyond the first interface arrival for this correlated population to become established. Increasing system size delays invasion but enhances the probability of ultimate successful stabilization. In two coupled SIR regions, transmission can initiate a macroscopic secondary outbreak, while permanent immunity restricts both epidemics to transient activity.

title: Semi-regular admixed arrays: asymptotic enumeration and when information is additive
summary: In genomic data analysis, admixed arrays are pairs of matrices recording the local ancestry and the allele at each position of the haplotypes of admixed individuals. We study two-way diploid admixed arrays with $N$ individuals and $P$ loci under two families of constraints: local ancestry tallies, which fix the number of ancestry assignments per individual, and ancestry-specific sums, which fix the allele count per locus and ancestry. These two constraint families correspond to summaries of admixed genetic data investigated in biomedical and genomic applications. In the semi-regular regime, where all tallies and sums are uniform, we use complex martingale techniques to derive asymptotic formulas for the number of doubly constrained arrays as $N$ and $P$ grow with bounded ratio, over the whole feasible region. The leading term is governed by the Shannon entropy of the frequencies of the four possible pairs of entries at a position of the two matrices; on the boundary one or two of them vanish, changing the Gaussian correction. We then ask whether the two families carry information additively, that is, whether an independence heuristic predicts the doubly constrained count up to a bounded factor. Measured against the smallest set of arrays defined by a constraint that each family implies on its own, additivity holds only on a set of measure zero. It includes an edge of the feasible region with correction factor $e^{-1/4}$, extending our earlier result at the symmetric point. Thus, how far the two summaries jointly narrow down individual-level ancestry and genotype configurations cannot generally be predicted from how far each does on its own.

title: Nutrient limitation drives Turing instabilities in cross-feeding microbial communities
summary: Microbial communities are shaped by metabolic interactions, often in the form of cross-feeding in which microbes exchange metabolites via diffusion through the environment. We show here that the diffusion of cross-fed metabolites generically leads to a Turing instability in resource-poor environments, driven by the feedback between local metabolite availability and cell growth. A coarse-grained model of community biomass identifies the few dimensionless parameters that control the instability, most notably the ratio of environmental energy supply to cellular maintenance costs. We find that the detailed topology of the metabolic interaction network can be coarse-grained into a single effective parameter to quantitatively characterise the instability. Beyond the onset of the instability, the community forms compact aggregates whose merger is prevented by a competition for shared resources. Overall, our results demonstrate how spatial structure can arise as an inevitable consequence of metabolic interactions in a microbial community.
